exercises.cue: Keep a clear center to each sound.
Aim the air steadily as the line rises to G.
Use the right-hand keys cleanly around E-flat.
Release the left index finger for middle D.
Keep C to D even inside the chromatic turn.
Give the rising figure a light tongue and one steady air stream.
Let the five notes ring evenly.
Keep the throat A light as the line turns.
Rock between G, G-sharp and throat A with small movements.
Hold throat A, then cover the holes together for clarion B.
Carry air through the B-flat to B-natural crossing.
Let the short notes bounce. Keep the air moving over the break.
Match the sound as you add and lift right-hand fingers.
Add the octave key as you move from C to D.
Keep the G-sharp pinky close to its key.
Coordinate the thumb and right hand on middle D.
Cross open C-sharp smoothly in both directions.
Start each short G cleanly and let the eighths travel.
Keep both hands curved as the notes rise.
Let the left hand lead the turn through B and C.
Place the B-flat and B-natural fingers deliberately.
Switch the octave key with the fingers from C to D.
Keep the thumb relaxed across C-sharp and D.
Connect the octave-key turn before adding speed.
Depress the valves fully with curved fingers.
Let the air carry F to the open G.
Move the valves together through F, F-sharp and G.
Listen for two centered pitches on open C and G.
Keep each valve change inside the pulse.
Give the opening call a clear attack and save air for the finish.
Hear the next pitch before each attack.
Sing the top of the arc before you play it.
Center the neighboring A-flat and A-natural.
Use the same F-side open fingering for written C, E and G.
Settle on the partial before changing direction.
Center the opening call, then tongue the answer lightly.
Arrive at each slide position on the beat.
Hear the upward line while the slide changes direction.
Keep the short slide moves around F precise.
Stay in first position for low B-flat and F above it.
Choose compact slide paths around E-flat, E and F.
Give the opening B-flat space, then move the slide quickly.
Match the attack as the valve combinations change.
Keep the sound full at the change of partial.
Keep the valve changes together around E-natural.
Match the open B-flat and F, then echo with first-valve notes.
Let the valve fingers follow the chromatic turn evenly.
Bounce off the short notes and connect the climbing run.
Alternate hands and strike near the center of each bar.
Look ahead to the turnaround bar.
Move to the raised bars with small, even strokes.
Aim the mallets before the skips and let each stroke rebound.
Trace the path between the two rows before adding speed.
Watch the next landing spot through the octave finish.
Alternate hands. Match the sound of your left and right strokes.
Keep the eighths even as the lead hand changes.
Echo a pair of right-hand strokes with a pair on the left.
Let each hand rebound for the double stroke.
Carry the double strokes through each change of direction.
Lift for the accents and keep the taps close to the head.
